title: KV-aware prefetch + adaptive fallback policy for OOM mitigation
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Add a coordinated OOM prevention and graceful-recovery system that combines KV-cache heatmap-aware prefetch/eviction, per-request memory budgeting, admission control for continuous batching, and staged fallback policies (quantization downgrade, context trimming, smaller model fallback). The goal is to reduce catastrophic OOMs, provide predictable degradation modes, and enable fast automated recovery without manual intervention.
updates: 2026-02-18: Initial ticket created after two customer incidents where 100% GPU utilization + large KV footprint caused host OOMs and request failures. Linked to runtime incident notes.

2026-02-25: Spike completed: prototype admission controller that rejects new batches when available GPU headroom < config.threshold. Observed 18% reduction in transient OOMs under synthetic heavy-KV workload. Notes in confluence: /r/inference/oom-spike-20260225.

2026-03-03: Design review with PM and SRE. Decided on three-tier fallback order: (1) soft admission + request-level trimming, (2) switch model execution path to 8-bit kernels, (3) fallback to smaller model variant. Added requirement for KV 'heat buckets' to drive smart eviction rather than LRU-only.

2026-03-08: Implementation work started for cache heatmap data structure and an API for runtime scheduler to query estimated KV memory for a given request. Implemented lightweight sampling in runtime to compute per-prefix reuse score.

2026-03-12: Integration test: combined admission + progressive quantization path. End-to-end test shows degraded but successful responses for >95% of previously failing requests (synthetic reproduction). Two flaky cases remain when huge multi-turn contexts with long-lived KV entries collide with large-batch spikes.
2026-03-14: Preparing rollout plan and dashboards. Added telemetry events for pre-oom triggers and fallback activation. Created feature-flag gating for per-tenant policy.
Notes: Updated_at reflects latest progress. See links for design doc and PRs.
decisions: Use heatmap-based KV eviction that weighs token reuse probability and token size rather than pure LRU.
Implement admission control at batch-formation time using estimated memory delta per request.

Fallback order: (1) admission + trimming, (2) quantization downgrade (dynamic 8-bit kernels), (3) reduce context window by prefix trimming with heuristic, (4) fallback to smaller compatible model variant, (5) return explicit 503 with retry-after if all else fails.
Expose per-tenant policy knobs in Console: memory_headroom_pct, fallback_sequence, max_trim_tokens, enable_progressive_quant.
Retries should be staged with exponential backoff and progressive warming: short warmup path to prefill KV on retry.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end synthetic repro (multi-tenant, heavy KV, large batches) shows >=90% request success rate under the same load that previously caused OOMs.
No increase in median latency > 10% for normal workloads when feature is enabled (telemetry baseline required).
Console shows per-tenant fallback activations and clear cost delta estimates for quantization fallbacks.
All fallback activations produce structured telemetry events and a single trace linking admission decision -> fallback steps -> final response.
Feature behind rollout feature flag; can be enabled per-tenant and globally revoked within 5 minutes.
test_plan: Unit tests for KV heatmap: reuse score computation, eviction ordering, and size accounting.
Load tests: run synthetic workloads that previously caused OOMs across all supported sequence lengths and batch sizes.
Chaos tests: kill a worker mid-eviction and observe graceful retry path.
Regression perf tests: ensure steady-state latencies not degraded for low-KV workloads.
Canary rollout to 5% of production tenants behind feature flag with telemetry gating (error_rate, fallback_rate thresholds).
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): Feature flag on in staging and perf cluster. Run full integration suite.
Phase 1 (canary): Enable for non-SLA tenants (5%) for 72 hours. Monitor fallback_rate, p95 latency, and SLO violations.
Phase 2 (expand): Gradual ramp to 25% then 50% with automated pause if fallback_rate > expected_threshold or p99 latency regresses.
Phase 3 (global): Enable by default for all new dedicated pools, and opt-in for existing; document recommended policy defaults.
Rollback: Feature flag off and disable admission controller within 5 minutes; ensure queued requests drain gracefully.
notes_for_reviewers: SRE/infra: please review the admission controller thresholds and default memory_headroom_pct=12%. We saw 12% balance latency vs safety in spike tests.
ML infra: validate quantization runtime path compatibility for trimmed contexts and ensure logits alignment across fallback models.
PM/Design: verify UX copy for Console when fallback triggers (suggested text in Confluence page).
